subject: Is data filtering and manipulating combination of several variables possible in Rattle?

messages.author: 491fff0079fc57d6
messages.subject: Is data filtering and manipulating combination of several variables possible in Rattle?
parts:
Is it possible in Rattle:

1) To filter out some records according to a filter when loading data-
set from a CSV file? In this case filter is a logical expression on
values of data-set variables. If not in Rattle, how to program this in
R?

2) To create a distribution of a combination of several variables? For
example, lets say we have x, y, z, p, q, t variables in some data-set.
Can I ask Rattle to build a distribution for all combinations of x and
y values in this data-set? If not in Rattle, how to program this in
R?

Thanks!

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: Is data filtering and manipulating combination of several variables possible in Rattle?
parts:
On Wednesday, March 27, 2013 8:39:39 AM UTC+11, dokondr wrote:
Is it possible in Rattle:

1) To filter out some records according to a filter when loading data-
set from a CSV file? In this case filter is a logical expression on
values of data-set variables. If not in Rattle, how to program this in
R?

Something like this....

Load the dataset into Rattle as usual.
Then in the R Console:
> ds <- subset(crs$dataset, x > 34 & q == "Yes")
(where x and q are Variables from your dataset)
Then in Rattle, choose the R Dataset option and select Data Name: "ds", then Execute

2) To create a distribution of a combination of several variables? For
example, lets say we have x, y, z, p, q, t variables in some data-set.
Can I ask Rattle to build a distribution for all combinations of x and
y values in this data-set? If not in Rattle, how to program this in
R?

Would probably need specific details of what you intended here. But perhaps this might be a hint:

Load data into Rattle as usual.
Then in the R Console:
> ds <- crs$dataset
> ds$NewVar <- (x + y^2)/z
Then in Rattle, choose the R Dataset option and select Data Name: "ds", then Execute.

You can explore the wealth of R expressions for the right one for the right hand side of the assignment above to match what you want.

Hope that helps.

Graham

parts:
I am probably the world's worst R programmer.
But I can give you a suggestion for your first question.

There are many ways to filter the data, but one that I think has the easiest syntax for newbies like me is the subset function.

If you want to subset records based on a logical filter, you use the function like this:

newDataFrame<-as.data.frame(subset(originalDataFrame,variableYouAreFilteringOn==1))

You could then select newDataFrame in rattle as your data source.

Ignore the following aside if you don't care:
-------------------------------------------------------

Just so you don't get confused if you look at the documentation for subset, it can also be used to filter which variables you want to keep in the dataset.

If you want to drop a few variables, the syntax is like this (notice the minus sign):

newDataFrame<-as.data.frame(subset(originalDataFrame,select=-c(firstVariableToDrop,secondVariableToDrop)))

If you want to only keep certain specified variables, the syntax is like this:

newDataFrame<-as.data.frame(subset(originalDataFrame,select=-c(firstVariableToDrop,secondVariableToDrop)))
-------------------------------------------------------

You can also use the bracket [] function to subset variables, which I do use occasionally, but I usually still use subset b/c the syntax is easier. Someone better at R can probably give an overview of using the bracket function.

I could stumble through manually creating a variable for all the combinations of x and y, but I don't think I'm the best to give you advice on that. Perhaps there is an elegant package that would make the task more straightforward.

Scott
